skills.name: Describe the chemical properties of sulphuric acid

note.text:
Dilute sulphuric acid behaves as a typical strong acid:
• with a metal above hydrogen: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2;
• with a base or basic oxide: CuO + H2SO4 → CuSO4 + H2O;
• with a carbonate: Na2CO3 + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + H2O + CO2.
Concentrated sulphuric acid has three further properties:
• Dehydrating agent: it removes hydrogen and oxygen as water. Sugar turns to a black spongy mass of carbon; blue copper(II) sulphate crystals turn white.
• Oxidising agent when hot: Cu + 2H2SO4 → CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O.
• A less volatile acid: it displaces more volatile acids from their salts. NaCl + H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HCl.
Safety: always add the acid to water, never water to the acid, because a great deal of heat is given out.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to describe dilute sulphuric acid as a typical acid and concentrated sulphuric acid as a dehydrating, oxidising and less volatile acid.
Builds on: Lesson {4} ({formula('SO2')} and the acid made from it) and Form Three acids, bases and salts.
Leads to: Lesson {9} (the uses of sulphur and its compounds) and salt preparations.

sections.heading: The dilute acid
The concentrated acid
sections.text:
Concentrated sulphuric acid has three extra properties:
• DEHYDRATING agent: it removes hydrogen and oxygen as water. Sugar becomes a black spongy mass of carbon; blue copper(II) sulphate crystals turn white; paper and wood char. It also dries gases that do not react with it.
• OXIDISING agent when hot: Cu + {2}{formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('CuSO4')} + {formula('SO2')} + {2}{formula('H2O')}. Copper is below hydrogen, so it could not react with the dilute acid at all.
• LESS VOLATILE acid: on heating it drives more volatile acids out of their salts: {formula('NaCl')} + {formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('NaHSO4')} + {formula('HCl')}.
Safety: always add the acid slowly to water with stirring, never water to the acid, because a great deal of heat is given out.

key_words.meaning: a substance that removes hydrogen and oxygen as water
a substance that gives oxygen to, or takes electrons from, another
water joined into a crystal, as in blue {formula('CuSO4')} crystals

mistake.wrong: copper reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to give hydrogen
mistake.right: copper does not react with the dilute acid at all
mistake.why: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series. Only the hot CONCENTRATED acid attacks it, giving {formula('SO2')}.

worked_example.problem: Explain what is seen when concentrated sulphuric acid is poured onto blue copper(II) sulphate crystals, and name the property shown.
steps: Blue copper(II) sulphate crystals contain water of crystallisation.
Concentrated sulphuric acid takes up water very strongly.
It removes the water from the crystals, and the solid turns white.
Removing water from a substance is dehydration, so the acid is acting as a dehydrating agent.
worked_example.answer: the blue crystals turn white; the acid is acting as a dehydrating agent

cards.idea: Dilute sulphuric acid is a typical acid: metal → hydrogen, base → salt and water, carbonate → carbon dioxide.
Concentrated sulphuric acid is a dehydrating agent: it removes water from other substances.

pick.q: Dilute sulphuric acid is added to zinc. What is seen?
pick.r: Bubbles of hydrogen, which pop with a lighted splint
e: Sulphur dioxide comes from the CONCENTRATED acid with copper, not from the dilute acid with zinc.
Sulphur is not formed with the dilute acid.
Zinc is above hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does react.
pick.y: Zn + {formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('ZnSO4')} + {formula('H2')}: the dilute acid behaves as an ordinary acid.

pick.q: Dilute sulphuric acid is added to sodium carbonate. What gas is given off?
pick.r: Carbon dioxide
e: Hydrogen comes from a metal with an acid, not from a carbonate.
Sulphur dioxide comes from a sulphite, not from a carbonate.
Hydrogen sulphide comes from a sulphide.
pick.y: {formula('Na2CO3')} + {formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('Na2SO4')} + {formula('H2O')} + {formula('CO2')}.

pick.q: Concentrated sulphuric acid is poured onto sugar. What is seen?
pick.r: The sugar turns black and a spongy mass of carbon rises out of the beaker
w: The sugar dissolves to give a clear solution
Nothing happens until the mixture is heated
e: The sugar is not simply dissolved; it is chemically changed.
The colour is black, from the carbon left behind.
The change starts at once, and heat is given out.
pick.y: The acid removes hydrogen and oxygen from the sugar as water, leaving carbon: it is a dehydrating agent.

pick.q: Copper is warmed with concentrated sulphuric acid. What gas is given off?
pick.r: Sulphur dioxide
e: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen.
Hydrogen sulphide comes from a sulphide with a dilute acid.
No oxygen is given off in this reaction.
pick.y: Cu + {2}{formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('CuSO4')} + {formula('SO2')} + {2}{formula('H2O')}: here the acid is an oxidising agent.

pick.q: Concentrated sulphuric acid is warmed with sodium chloride. What is given off, and why?
pick.r: Hydrogen chloride, because the acid is less volatile and displaces the more volatile acid
w: Chlorine, because the acid is an oxidising agent
Hydrogen, because sodium is a reactive metal
Nothing: the two do not react
e: Chlorine needs a stronger oxidising agent, such as manganese(IV) oxide with concentrated hydrochloric acid.
The sodium is already combined as a salt, so it cannot displace hydrogen.
The reaction is the standard preparation of hydrogen chloride.
pick.y: {formula('NaCl')} + {formula('H2SO4')} → {formula('NaHSO4')} + {formula('HCl')}: a less volatile acid drives out a more volatile one.

pick.q: Why must concentrated sulphuric acid be added to water, and never water to the acid?
pick.r: Mixing gives out a great deal of heat, and water poured onto the acid can boil and spit acid out
w: The acid would become too weak
Water would react chemically with the acid to give hydrogen
e: Diluting always lowers the concentration; that is not the danger.
No hydrogen is given off; the danger is heat.
The order matters a great deal for safety.
pick.y: Adding acid slowly to a large volume of water lets the heat spread out safely.
